title: Pressure scenarios
subject: PSHE
source: Written for pshe/y8 lesson 2 (Pressure scenarios (pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 2: Peer influence and risky substances. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

panels.title: Risks
points: Smoking: cancer, heart and lung disease
Vaping: nicotine addiction; long-term effects still being studied
Alcohol: harms the developing brain, liver

panels.title: The law
points: Illegal to sell tobacco or vapes to under-18s
Illegal to sell alcohol to under-18s
Many drugs are illegal for everyone (Misuse of Drugs Act 1971)

model.title: A friend offers a vape: 'Everyone's doing it.'

parts.text: Clear no: 'No thanks, I'm not into that.'
Reason: 'It's addictive and it's against my faith.'
Change subject: 'Want to play football instead?'
If pressure continues: leave and tell an adult

blocks.h: Pressure scenarios: write a refusal and an exit

questions.q: Older pupils at the park offer you a vape and say 'Everyone does it'.
questions.a: Refusal: 'No thanks, it's not for me.' Exit: 'I've got to get home for Maghrib' and leave.

questions.q: A friend dares you to climb onto a garage roof to get a ball.
questions.a: Refusal: 'No, it's not safe.' Exit: suggest asking the owner or an adult, and walk away.

questions.q: A group chat member asks for your account password 'just to check something'.
questions.a: Refusal: 'I never share passwords.' Exit: leave the chat; tell a parent.

questions.q: Friends want you to come with them instead of going to your Qur'an class.
questions.a: Refusal: 'I'm going to my class.' Exit: offer to meet afterwards.

keywords.def: the effect friends and others our age have on our choices
an addictive drug in cigarettes and most vapes
being unable to stop doing or using something
the UK law that makes some drugs illegal

questions.q: Write a refusal line for 'Just try one sip.'
questions.a: 'No thanks, I don't drink.' and change the subject.

questions.q: Core: Pressure scenarios (pupil PDF): write a refusal and an exit for each.
Extend: In the portal response box, explain why 'everyone does it' is misleading. Start: 'Most young people...'
questions.a: Most young people do not vape or drink regularly; influence makes it seem more common than it is.

questions.q: Stretch: Explain how Islamic teaching and UK law both protect young people from substances.
questions.a: Islam forbids intoxicants and self-harm; UK law sets age limits and bans some drugs.

questions.q: The legal age to buy alcohol or vapes in the UK is...
questions.a: C) 18. It is illegal to sell either to under-18s.

questions.q: Nicotine is... A) a vitamin B) an addictive drug C) a type of water
Big question: why do people do things in a group they would not do alone?
questions.a: To fit in and avoid being left out: peer influence.
